title: BlockchainAnchor
description: A Merkle root over a batch of salted record hashes, committed to an external ledger. SPECIFIED, NOT IMPLEMENTED — no chain integration exists in this repository. An anchor proves existence-before-a-time and non-alteration-since. It proves NOTHING about whether the anchored record was accurate. Chain-neutral and optional: a deployment that anchors nothing is fully conforming. NO PERSONAL DATA EVER ENTERS AN ANCHOR — no payload, no person-resolving identifier, and no hash of a low-entropy personal value (which would be a lookup table, not a pseudonym).

serialisation_version.description: Canonical serialisation version. Versioned independently, because changing it invalidates prior proofs — old proofs MUST remain verifiable under the old version.

batch_size.description: Records in the batch. One transaction per event is NOT the model: it makes cost scale with citizen activity and turns the ledger into a timing side-channel.

chain.description: Chain-neutral. No chain is named by the protocol; this records which ledger a given deployment used. Multi-chain anchoring of the same root is supported and recommended as a hedge.

InclusionProof.title: InclusionProof
InclusionProof.description: What a verifier needs to check one record against an anchor WITHOUT trusting IDauto: recompute the leaf hash from the canonical bytes and salt, walk the path, compare to the on-chain root. The salt is per-record and never published — without it, a low-entropy record is brute-forceable from its hash.
